pages.alt: A half-wave rectifier: one diode, D1, between supply wire A and the top of a resistor load. At 360°, no current flows. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: One diode
pages.text: With the cursor at the end of the cycle, the output shows one hump in the positive half. In the negative half it is a flat line. The arrow through the load shows only during the hump.

pages.alt: A half-wave rectifier: one diode, D1, between supply wire A and the top of a resistor load. At 360°, no current flows. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: The average at the end
options: 0 V, as the second half is empty
pages.task: At 180° the average reads 207 V. What will the average read at 360°, the end of the cycle?
pages.why: The flat half adds no area but doubles the length. So the average halves, to about 104 V. That is 0.318 of the 325 V peak, the peak ÷ π.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 270°, D3 and D4 conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 270 degrees.
pages.name: Four diodes
pages.text: In the positive half, D1 and D2 are bold. In the negative half, D3 and D4 are bold. Both times the arrow through the load points down.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 270°, D3 and D4 conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 270 degrees.
pages.answer: Down, the same way as in the positive half
pages.name: Which way now?
options: Up, as the supply has reversed
None, as only D1 and D2 ever conduct
Down, the same way as in the positive half
pages.task: Which way does current flow through the load now?
pages.why: In the negative half, the supply's other wire is the high one. D3 takes the current to the top of the load. D4 returns it from the bottom. So it flows down, as before. Each pair conducts while the other blocks.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 360°, D3 and D4 conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: Twice the average
pages.text: Over a whole cycle the bridge shows two humps. Its average line settles at 207 V, twice the half-wave's 104 V.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 90°, D1 and D2 conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 90 degrees.
pages.name: What the diodes take
pages.task: A bridge feeds a 12 V battery charger. How much lower is its output than with perfect diodes?
pages.why: At every moment the current passes through two diodes in series. Each holds about 0.7 V. So the bridge takes about 1.4 V. On a 207 V output that is under 1%. On 12 V it is about 12%.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 360°, D3 and D4 conduct, and current flows down through the load. A probe is clipped across D1. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees. Below, the probe's trace shows the voltage across the probed diode the wrong way round.
pages.name: The probe
pages.text: The probe's trace sits on zero while D1 conducts. In the negative half it climbs to 325 V at 270° and falls back to zero at 360°.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. At 360°, D3 and D4 conduct, and current flows down through the load. A probe is clipped across D1. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees. Below, the probe's trace shows the voltage across the probed diode the wrong way round.
pages.name: A 115 V bridge
options: None, as a blocked diode carries no current
pages.task: A bridge runs from a 115 V single-phase supply. What reverse voltage must each diode withstand?
pages.why: While a diode blocks, the conducting pair joins it straight across the supply. So it holds the whole supply the wrong way round. At the peak that is 115 × √2 = 163 V. Its peak inverse voltage must be above that.

pages.alt: A six-pulse rectifier: three lines, L1 to L3, each with an upper and a lower diode, feeding a resistor load. At 360°, L3's upper diode and L2's lower diode conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The six line-to-line waves are drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: Six diodes
pages.text: The six line-to-line waves are drawn pale. The output rides their tops. The bold pair changes every 60°. The arrow through the load points down throughout.

pages.alt: A six-pulse rectifier: three lines, L1 to L3, each with an upper and a lower diode, feeding a resistor load. At 360°, L3's upper diode and L2's lower diode conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The six line-to-line waves are drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: How low it dips
pages.task: On 400 V the line-to-line peak is 566 V. Each top of the output runs from 30° before a peak to 30° after it. How low does the output dip?
pages.why: Each top is a slice of a cosine, from −30° to +30°. At its edges it has fallen to cos 30° = 0.866 of the peak. So the output dips only to 0.866 × 566 = 490 V.

pages.alt: A six-pulse rectifier: three lines, L1 to L3, each with an upper and a lower diode, feeding a resistor load. At 360°, L3's upper diode and L2's lower diode conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The six line-to-line waves are drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: Where 1.35 comes from
pages.text: On 400 V the average line settles at 540 V, close under the 566 V tops.

pages.alt: A bridge rectifier: four diodes, D1 to D4, in a diamond between an AC supply and a resistor load. D3 has failed open. At 360°, no current flows. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The supply is drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.answer: Half-wave: about 104 V, 50 humps a second
pages.name: One diode fails
options: Half-wave: about 104 V, 50 humps a second
As before: 207 V, 100 humps a second
Nothing: 0 V, as the bridge is broken
pages.task: One diode in a 230 V, 50 Hz bridge fails open. What does the load get now?
pages.why: The pair with the open diode can no longer carry its half. The other pair still carries its half. So the bridge works as a half-wave rectifier. The average falls to about 104 V. The humps come 50 times a second.

pages.alt: A six-pulse rectifier: three lines, L1 to L3, each with an upper and a lower diode, feeding a resistor load. At 360°, L3's upper diode and L2's lower diode conduct, and current flows down through the load. One supply cycle, 0 to 360 degrees. The six line-to-line waves are drawn pale. The output, the area under it and its average are drawn up to the time cursor at 360 degrees.
pages.name: Six-pulse on 440 V
pages.task: A six-pulse rectifier runs from 440 V into a resistor. What average DC does the load get?
pages.why: The average is 1.35 times the line voltage. That gives 1.35 × 440 = 594 V. The tops reach 440 × √2 = 622 V. The dips between them pull the average a little below that.
